title: Frontend Page Rendering with PAGEVIEW

hints.text: A page is rendered by the PAGEVIEW content object: `page.<n> = PAGEVIEW`, with the paths under the same key — `page.<n>.paths.<n> = EXT:<ext>/Resources/Private/`. FLUIDTEMPLATE is the predecessor and still resolves file., templateName. and its own root paths; PAGEVIEW deliberately does none of that.

One `paths` entry becomes three roots: the configured path plus Pages/ for templates, plus Partials/, plus Layouts/. There is no separate templateRootPaths, partialRootPaths or layoutRootPaths to set.

The template name is not configurable. It is the page layout identifier with the pagets__ prefix stripped, and "default" where the page declares none — so backend_layout = pagets__landingpage renders Pages/Landingpage and nothing else will.

hints: page-content-areas belongs before the template is written: an identifier the layout never declared is not an empty column, it is HTTP 500 on every page. page-variables-and-processors has the two that bite later — PAGEVIEW rejecting a variables. entry whose name it assigns itself, and a menu excludeDoktypes list that replaces the default rather than adding to it and puts every storage folder in the navigation. page-cache-headers is the page that is right in curl and wrong in the browser.

title: What a Frontend Request Fills and Clears in PageRenderer
hints: The renderer is filled in one order and emptied in another, and a diff on either class is read against that order. `RequestHandler::generatePageBodyContent()` goes first and touches the renderer not at all: it renders the cacheable body from the page TypoScript and leaves a placeholder where each USER_INT and COA_INT sits.

`config.disableAllHeaderCode` returns from `generatePageContent()` at that point, before anything populates the renderer and before anything renders it, so the body is the whole response and the renderer stays empty for the rest of the request.

`processHtmlBasedRenderingSettings()` is the phase that fills the head — doctype, the html and head tags, the favicon, the CSS and JavaScript the page TypoScript includes, headerData, footerData, the title, the inline settings and the inline language labels — and it adds the body tag through `addBodyContent()`. `generatePageContent()` appends the page content with the same call afterwards, so `bodyContent` is the body tag followed by the content, in that order.

hints.text: Then one of two exits. A page with no uncached content elements is rendered whole by `renderFrontendPage()` — the frontend's own, beside `render()` which is the backend's — and that call resets the renderer as its last step.
Then one of two exits. A page with no uncached content elements is rendered whole by `render()`, which serves the backend and the frontend both, and that call resets the renderer as its last step.

hints: The other exit is `renderPageWithUncachedObjects()`, which writes a placeholder comment for every head marker and deliberately does not reset: the renderer is serialised whole and cached beside the content, to be picked up again when the uncached objects run. `getState()` is what is serialised — every property of the renderer, plus the meta tag registry's state and the JavaScript renderer's, minus the injected services.

hints.text: That state is the `pageRendererState` entry of the page cache row, and the `PrepareTypoScriptFrontendRendering` middleware restores it with `updateState()` on a cache hit.
That state is `config['INTincScript_ext']['pageRendererState']` on TypoScriptFrontendController, and `INTincScript()` restores it with `updateState()` before it substitutes anything.

hints: The uncached objects then run with that whole state populated rather than with an empty renderer, which is why an asset a USER_INT registers is added on top of what the cached page already carried. `renderJavaScriptAndCssForProcessingOfUncachedContentObjects()` substitutes the head placeholders last, and resets at the end of it.

hints.text: `renderPageWithUncachedObjects()` empties `bodyContent` before it returns, so the body is cached as the content and not a second time inside the serialised state.

`renderPageWithUncachedObjects()` leaves `bodyContent` standing, so the body is cached twice — once as the content, once inside the serialised state — and a render that follows it on the same instance starts from that body rather than from an empty one.

hints: `reset()` is not the mirror image of what filled the renderer, and the leftovers are where a page ends up wearing the previous one's head. It clears `bodyContent`, the JavaScript and CSS files and inline blocks, `jsLibs`, the inline comments, headerData, footerData, the locale, the doctype, the template file and the JavaScript renderer. It does not clear `cssLibs`, the title, the favicon, the inline settings or the inline language labels, and the meta tag registry is a service of its own that nothing in `reset()` touches — so a meta tag set for one page is still set for whatever renders next in the same process.

hints.text: `reset()` does not clear `bodyContent` on this line either: the property is only ever overwritten by `setBodyContent()`, so every render after the first starts from what the one before it left.

hints: This is the state the request holds, not which template produced the body: frontend-page-rendering answers that one, and typo3_rule_lookup(documentId "core/testing/proving-a-rendering") is how a rendering is proved.

title: Addressing a Content Area in a Page Template
appliesTo: contentArea argument must be an instance of

hints.text: The content of the page arrives as one variable holding the content areas, named by the `contentAs` option and "content" by default. A single area is addressed as {content.<identifier>} and rendered with <f:render.contentArea contentArea="{content.main}" />.
PAGEVIEW hands the template no content areas of its own. dataProcessing.<n> = page-content puts them into the variable its option as names, content by default.
A page-content data processor beside PAGEVIEW is redundant. It runs after PAGEVIEW has assigned the areas and replaces that variable with its own result.
Those identifiers are the ones the page layout declares for its columns in mod.web_layout.BackendLayouts — see the site set hints.

An identifier the layout never declared resolves to nothing, and f:render.contentArea handed that nothing throws rather than rendering nothing: the argument is registered as a ContentArea, an absent one falls back to the tag's children, and neither of those is one. It is an InvalidArgumentValueException, exception 1770212183, and it is HTTP 500 on every page the template renders — so a mistyped identifier fails exactly like a column the layout has not got.
A declared column holding no content elements is the case that renders empty and reports nothing: the area is there with no records in it, and the ViewHelper answers with the empty string.
A column the layout declares without an explicit identifier is keyed on the md5 of the layout identifier and the colPos and raises a deprecation, so the area exists and no template can name it.
A column the layout declares without an explicit identifier is refused while the page layout is resolved, exception 1780173420, so the page fails before any template is reached.

title: What a Page Template Is Handed

hints.text: The site set settings are assigned as {settings.<path>}, nested at each dot: a setting defined as sitepackage.brandName reads as {settings.sitepackage.brandName}. PAGEVIEW assigns `site`, `language` and `page` itself and rejects a variables. entry that uses one of those names.

The title the site configuration states is {site.configuration.websiteTitle}, and the title one language states is {language.websiteTitle}. A language that sets none leaves its own empty rather than inherit the site's, so a header reads the language's and falls back to the site's.
Data processors are configured on the PAGEVIEW object as dataProcessing., the same way FLUIDTEMPLATE takes them.

hints: The navigation is one of them: `dataProcessing.<n> = menu`. Its excludeDoktypes option replaces the default list instead of adding to it, and that default — PageRepository::DOKTYPE_BE_USER_SECTION and DOKTYPE_SYSFOLDER — is what keeps backend user sections and storage folders out of the menu. A configured list has to repeat both of those doktype values, or every storage folder ends up in the navigation: no error, nothing logged, and not visible until the site gets its first folder below the root page.

title: How the Content Elements on a Page Are Rendered
hints: The content elements on that page are rendered by lib.contentElement, which is a FLUIDTEMPLATE of its own with its own template, partial and layout roots — fluid_styled_content's by default, extended through the styles.templates settings. Pointing one of those roots at the directory PAGEVIEW resolves its own templates from is what makes the page frame collide with the content element frame; the sitepackage layout hint has the naming that keeps them apart.

title: What a Row Handed to lib.contentElement Must Carry

hints.text: lib.contentElement runs the record-transformation data processor over its own data before it renders, so an array reaching it is built into a Record by RecordFactory and offered to the template as record, beside the untouched data. A row assembled in PHP and handed over with f:cObject — a view helper putting a handful of keys together for a plugin — therefore has to be a whole row now, and one that rendered before is refused outright.

Name the table on the call. f:cObject hands its table argument to ContentObjectRenderer::start(), the processor falls back to that current table, and an empty one reaches RecordFactory as no table at all: InvalidArgumentException, exception 1715266929, "Unable to create Record from non-TCA table". The row also owes the typeField — CType for tt_content — or createRawRecord() throws exception 1715267513 before it looks at a single field. uid and pid are the only two it does without; both fall back to 0.

What it does owe is every field TCA[ctrl] declares a capability for, guarded in three places that throw IncompleteRecordException one after the other: exception 1726046917 for the language fields, exception 1726046918 for the workspace fields, and exception 1726046919 for each system capability in turn. Every message names one field, so adding the field the message asks for buys exactly one more attempt — read the whole list instead.

For tt_content that list is sys_language_uid and l18n_parent; t3ver_wsid, t3ver_oid, t3ver_state and t3ver_stage; and crdate, tstamp, starttime, endtime, deleted, hidden, editlock, sorting, fe_group and rowDescription. l10n_source is asked for with has() and may be left out; l18n_diffsource and l10n_state are stripped and never read. Another table's list is its own ctrl read the same way.

The values are typed, and a wrong one throws TypeError rather than the exception above — which is what makes the last stretch of this look like a different bug. crdate, tstamp, starttime and endtime go to DateTimeFactory::createFromTimestamp(int), so an integer passes where a numeric string fails; fe_group goes through GeneralUtility::intExplode() and has to be a string, so '0' passes where 0 fails; rowDescription is typed as a string. The rest are cast and take any scalar — the language, workspace and sorting fields to int, deleted, hidden and editlock to bool.

What such a Record then hands the template, and which fields it moves out of the row into _system, is record-system-properties. The template, partial and layout roots it renders through are page-content-element-rendering.

title: What a Cacheable Page Template Answers With
appliesTo: page is cached in the browser
hints: config.sendCacheHeaders answers a cacheable page with the page cache lifetime as its max-age and an Expires to match — for a page with nothing that expires that is close to a year out. It is suppressed while a backend user is logged in, which is why it bites exactly where nobody is: a browser that has such a response will not ask again, so a fixed template keeps rendering the old page and flushing the server cache changes nothing. Bind it to the application context — [applicationContext == "Development"] config.sendCacheHeaders = 0 [END] — and read "it is right in curl and wrong in the browser" as the response headers rather than as a bug in the code.

title: Which Caches a Change Invalidates, and What Clears the Rest
hints: A changed Fluid template recompiles itself and needs no command for that. The identifier a compiled template is stored under is a hash of the file path and the file's modification time — createIdentifierForFile() in typo3fluid/fluid's TemplatePaths, the same mechanism in every Fluid release the covered majors pin — so an edited template, partial or layout is written under a new identifier and the stale entry is never read again. Deleting var/cache/code/fluid_template by hand removes entries nothing would have asked for, and it is not what makes an edit appear.

What still answers with the old page is the page cache, and it is in another group. Its identifier is built from the page id and type, the user's groups, the site, the language base, the route arguments, the sys_template rows and the TypoScript condition lists; no template file enters it, so a cacheable page keeps serving what it rendered before. `typo3 cache:flush --group=pages` is what a frontend template change needs. A backend module has no page cache in front of it and shows the edit on the next request.

That group is mostly not on disk. pages, hash and rootline are Typo3DatabaseBackend caches, in the tables cache_pages, cache_hash and cache_rootline, so nothing deleted under var/cache/ reaches any of them — typoscript is the one file-backed cache in the group, and a file deletion that misses the rest leaves the rendered output exactly where it was.

TypoScript clears itself where it is a record and does not where it is a file. The typoscript cache keys a sys_template row on a hash of that row's own constants, config and include fields, so editing the record invalidates it; an @import target or an include_static_file set is keyed on the file name alone, so an edited .typoscript file in an extension keeps its parsed include tree until group pages is flushed.

A TCA change needs group system. The compiled TCA sits in the core cache under an identifier made of the TYPO3 version, the project path and the installed package list, so nothing about a Configuration/TCA or TCA/Overrides file enters it and the old TCA is served until `typo3 cache:flush --group=system`.

A change to the wiring needs group di. The compiled container is cached under an identifier made of the TYPO3 version, the project path and the installed package list, in every application context. No class and no Configuration/Services.yaml or Services.php enters it. So a new constructor argument, a changed service definition and an attribute the container autoconfigures, such as #[AsCommand], reach the running instance only after `typo3 cache:flush --group=di`. Until then a constructor that gained a parameter fails with «Too few arguments to function ...::__construct()», and a new service is not found.

`typo3 cache:flush` takes --group with system, pages, di or all and defaults to all, which is the one to reach for when the change touched more than one of them. di is not a group like the others — it has no cacheConfigurations entry, the command flushes the dependency injection container backend itself, and it does so for system and all as well. `typo3 cache:warmup` takes the same groups, for a deployment where the first request must not pay for the rebuild.

hints.text: `typo3 cache:flushtags <tags>` flushes by tag rather than by group, narrowed with --groups. Where the core has no such command, flushing by tag is reachable only through CacheManager.

A component's definition does not follow its own template. fluid_component_definitions keys a component on its namespace and view helper name and on nothing else, so a changed argument or slot declaration needs group system — even though the same file's compiled template clears itself.

hints: Its neighbour is page-cache-headers, for the page that is still wrong after every one of these: that one is not a server cache at all.
